content: Carbamide is an over-the-counter (OTC) emollient that has been approved by the FDA for the treatment of excessive ear wax. It is commonly used to soften, loosen, and facilitate the removal of ear wax. The active ingredient in this product is carbamide peroxide at a concentration of 6.5%. Inactive ingredients include glycerin, oxyquinoline, aloe barbadensis leaf extract, and anthemis nobilis flower oil. Indications and Dosage for Adults: Carbamide is intended for occasional use to assist in softening and removing excessive ear wax. For adults and children over the age of 12, the recommended dosage is as follows: Tilt the head sideways and instill 5 to 10 drops of the solution into the affected ear. Keep the drops in the ear for several minutes by maintaining the head in a tilted position or by placing a cotton ball in the ear. This process can be repeated twice daily for up to four days, or as directed by a healthcare provider. Any residual wax may be removed by gently flushing the ear with warm water using a soft rubber bulb ear syringe. For children under the age of 12, consultation with a healthcare provider is recommended before use. Pediatric Use: The dosage and indications for pediatric patients over the age of 12 are the same as those for adults. For children under 12 years of age, a healthcare provider should be consulted prior to use. Contraindications and Warnings: Carbamide should not be used in the following situations: If there is ear drainage, discharge, pain, irritation, or a rash in the ear. If the patient experiences dizziness. If there is a known injury or perforation (hole) in the eardrum, or if the patient has undergone ear surgery, unless directed by a healthcare provider. For more than four consecutive days. When using this product, avoid contact with the eyes. If accidental contact with the eyes occurs, flush the eyes with water and consult a healthcare provider. If excessive ear wax remains after four consecutive days of use, discontinue the product and seek medical advice. Keep this product out of the reach of children. If swallowed, seek immediate medical attention or contact a Poison Control Center. Adverse Reactions: The most commonly reported adverse reaction is an allergic response. There is limited information available regarding adverse reactions observed during post-marketing surveillance. Use in Specific Populations: Pregnancy and Nursing Mothers: There is no specific FDA guidance on the use of carbamide during pregnancy, labor, delivery, or while breastfeeding. Pediatric and Geriatric Use: There is no specific FDA guidance on the use of carbamide in pediatric patients under 12 years of age or in geriatric populations. Renal and Hepatic Impairment: There is no specific FDA guidance on the use of carbamide in patients with renal or hepatic impairment. Gender, Race, and Immunocompromised Patients: There is no specific FDA guidance on the use of carbamide in relation to gender, race, or immunocompromised status. Administration: Carbamide is administered topically as ear drops. Monitoring: There is limited information available regarding the monitoring of patients using carbamide. Mechanism of Action: The mechanism of action of carbamide peroxide is not fully detailed in the drug label. Precautions with Alcohol: The interaction between alcohol and carbamide has not been established. Patients should consult their healthcare provider regarding the use of alcohol while using this medication. Brand Names: Carbamide peroxide is marketed under the brand name Ear Wax Removing Drops. Packaging: The product is often supplied as part of an ear wax cleansing kit, which includes ear wax removing drops and an ear cleansing spray.
